verdict_reason: The one value-changing code defect I found last pass is fixed and I verified the fix: `rel_tol = S[0] * max(X.shape) * eps` now agrees with numpy exactly -- on real gpt2 last-layer states the shipped rank is 763 and np.linalg.matrix_rank(Xc) is 763, where the old `max(S.shape)` convention gave 764 and cond_number 8999.41 against the correct 3986.25. The other two quantities are exact: avg_cosine_similarity's closed form (N||mean(unit)||^2 - 1)/(N-1) matches brute-force all-ordered-distinct-pairs to 1.18e-07 over 20 random shapes, and it reproduces Ethayarajh's OWN released per-layer numbers on his OWN corpus to Pearson 0.9939 across 13 layers (layer 12: 0.9713 vs his committed 0.978, 0.68% relative). effective_rank is the shared Roy & Vetterli helper on raw sigma. svd_auc is a BLME construct with no source, but it computes exactly what it says (verified against its closed form: a rank-1 cloud gives (D-1)/D exactly at D = 2, 4, 8, 22).
comparable_reason: Measured on 20 stored models (results/blme, d_model 512-2560). effective_rank is essentially d_model: Pearson r = +0.953 (p < 1e-9) on the raw value, range 191-1996 -- a raw dimension count, not comparable. cond_number spans 50.25 to 2.46e8 across the zoo, five orders of magnitude, and is not a bounded quantity. avg_cosine_similarity is genuinely comparable (r = -0.372, p = 0.11, range -0.009..0.055 in the stale sweep; 0.92-0.95 on current code) -- it is a mean cosine, dimensionless and bounded. participation_ratio raw is clean (r = +0.011, p = 0.96) but is dropped from the feature matrix as an exact duplicate of geometry_isoscore.isoscore_effective_dims. svd_auc raw is flat in width (r = -0.015, p = 0.95) but its CEILING is (D-1)/D, so on gpt2 the entire informative range is the last 0.5% (measured 0.994350 against a 0.998698 ceiling).
normalized_variant: effective_rank_norm, participation_ratio_norm (emitted by beyond_benchmarks/scripts/aggregate_results.py NORMALIZATIONS, not by the task)
github_reason: Located and fetched kawine/contextual (Ethayarajh's released code): analyze.py, preprocess.py, sts.csv and the authors' committed gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json. I could NOT execute their pipeline -- it needs allennlp, spacy and the Python-3.6-era pytorch_pretrained package with an HDF5 intermediate -- so this is PARTIAL on the run. But I did cross-verify numerically: analyze.py's explore_embedding_space samples 1000 sentences and takes ONE uniformly random word from each, then averages the pairwise cosine, which is the same estimand as BLME's closed form over distinct pairs. Running that protocol on their own sts.csv with HF gpt2 reproduces their committed 'mean cosine similarity across words' layer by layer: 0.6171/0.6474/0.5572/0.5906/0.5638/0.5667/0.5629/0.5725/0.5905/0.6123/0.6426/0.7454/0.9713 against their 0.611/0.644/0.597/0.614/0.587/0.573/0.578/0.582/0.595/0.617/0.667/0.758/0.978 -- Pearson 0.9939. No reference implementation exists for effective_rank, svd_auc or cond_number as assembled here.
paper_reason: Ethayarajh 2019 Fig. 1 / Sec. 4.1 states that in GPT-2's last layer two randomly sampled words have an average cosine similarity of ~0.99, and the authors' released gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json pins it at 0.978. BLME's anisotropy kernel, run under the paper's own sampling protocol (one random word per sentence) on the paper's own sts.csv, gives 0.9713 -- relative error 0.68%. The full 13-layer profile matches at Pearson 0.9939 including the paper's headline qualitative finding, the sharp last-layer jump (0.745 -> 0.971 measured, 0.758 -> 0.978 published). On the study's own WikiText corpus the same estimator gives 0.9510 (one word per sentence, N=1000) and 0.9392 (all tokens, N=100,740), so the corpus, not the estimator, is the source of the remaining gap.
confounds_reason: effective_rank is a raw dimension count and correlates r = +0.953 with d_model over 20 stored models -- it IS width, to a first approximation. cond_number is unbounded and spans 50 to 2.5e8. svd_auc's ceiling is (D-1)/D exactly (verified: 0.500 at D=2, 0.750 at D=4, 0.875 at D=8, 0.954545 at D=22), so a wider model's score is compressed into a narrower band near 1 even for identical spectral shape -- a structural width dependence, though empirically the measured values are flat in width (r = -0.015). avg_cosine_similarity and participation_ratio are the two clean ones (r = -0.372 and +0.011).
defects: STUDY-SIDE MIS-NORMALIZATION, AND THE DUPLICATE RULE DOES NOT COVER IT. aggregate_results.NORMALIZATIONS still applies div_dmodel to participation_ratio. Re-measured on 20 stored models: raw participation_ratio has r(d_model) = +0.011 (p = 0.96) and dividing by d_model INTRODUCES r = -0.488 (p = 0.029). Worse, feature_selection.DROP_AS_DUPLICATE matches the exact column name 'geometry_svd.participation_ratio', so the raw duplicate is dropped while the derived 'geometry_svd.participation_ratio_norm' that aggregate_results creates survives -- the harmful twin is the one that reaches the regression. effective_rank_norm is fine and should stay (+0.953 -> +0.282).

participation_ratio still adds a fixed +1e-12 to its denominator, which breaks the scale invariance the quantity is defined to have. Re-measured on a 300x5 matrix: PR = 1.796281 at scale 1 and 1.796282 at 1e-3, but 0.600092 at 1e-5, 0.000090 at 1e-6 and 0.000000 at 1e-7, while effective_rank is 3.1745 at every scale. LATENT at the shipped protocol (real gpt2 sum lambda^2 is ~9.4e7) but it should be an explicit `if sum_eig_sq == 0: nan` guard, not an epsilon.

svd_auc has no cited source and its scale is set by the ambient dimension: for a rank-1 cloud it is exactly (D-1)/D (verified 0.500000 / 0.750000 / 0.875000 / 0.954545 at D = 2 / 4 / 8 / 22), so on gpt2 the whole informative range is the last 0.5% (0.994350 measured against a 0.998698 ceiling). Either delete it or define it against an explicit ambient-dimension policy and document the ceiling.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR VERDICT: I wrote that the per-layer branch is dead because defaults.yaml has layerwise: false. That is wrong. beyond_benchmarks/configs/tasks.yaml:184 sets `geometry_svd: {num_samples: 200, layerwise: true}` and config_loader.resolve_task_config gives user overrides priority over defaults.yaml, so the layerwise branch IS what the study runs. Its `last_key = layer_{max(all_layers.keys())}` is the post-final-norm entry, which is the right layer for Ethayarajh's Eq. 4 (his layer 12 is post-norm too, confirmed by the head-to-head above) but is worth documenting, since the same index is the WRONG layer for the transition-style tasks that utils.collected_layer_count now trims.

The cache and non-cache paths still build different populations. Running the task with cache=None at num_samples=200 gives N = 2,000 (collect_hidden_states subsamples <= 10 tokens per document in single-layer mode) against ~23,000 on the cache path, and cond_number is strongly N-dependent. Any model run without a populated cache is incommensurable with the rest of the sweep.
